'''''Indigofera decora''''', commonly known as '''summer wisteria''', is a [[Specific epithet (botany)|species]] of [[shrub]] native to [[China]] and [[Japan]] that has since been introduced to [[Australia]] and [[Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Indigofera incarnata (Willd.) Nakai {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:499488-1|access-date=2021-03-08|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref> A member of the [[genus]] ''[[Indigofera]]'', its family is [[Fabaceae]]<ref name="CoL">{{cite web|url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/col/details/species/id/e90a49b7f674b059ca98533a9872fb3d|title=Species Details : Indigofera decora Lindl.|access-date=26 January 2019|website=[[Catalogue of Life]]}}</ref> and is used primarily for decorative purposes,<ref name="Missouribotgrdn">{{cite web|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=e382|title=Indigofera decora|work=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]]|access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref> though it has also been used to make indigo-colored dye.<ref name=":0" />

''I. decora'' is a [[deciduous]], spreading shrub. It often grows 1–2.5 feet tall and 3-4 feet wide. It features compound, pinnate [[Leaf|leaves]] up to 8 inches long with 7-13 elliptic, dark green leaflets. In the [[summer]], it produces axillary [[Raceme|racemes]] of light pink or purple [[Pea|pea-like]] [[Flower|flowers]].<ref name="Missouribotgrdn" /> Each raceme may boast twenty to forty flowers, and the [[Calyx (botany)|calyxes]] have broadly triangular lobes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Indigofera decora - Trees and Shrubs Online|url=https://treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/indigofera/indigofera-decora/|access-date=2021-03-08|website=treesandshrubsonline.org}}</ref>

''I. decora'' is best suited to well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soils. It is somewhat heat and drought tolerant, but benefits from afternoon shade in hot, humid environments. It is cold hardy in the [[United States|US]] in [[Hardiness zone|zones]] 7–11.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Indigofera incarnata (Chinese Indigo) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/indigofera-incarnata/|access-date=2021-03-08|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>

==Varieties==
There are three recognised varieties of ''Indigofera decora'':<ref name="CoL"/>
* Indigofera decora var. chalara ([[William Grant Craib|Craib]]) Y.Y.Fang & C.Z.Zheng
* Indigofera decora var. cooperi ([[William Grant Craib|Craib]]) Y.Y.Fang & C.Z.Zheng
* Indigofera decora var. ichangensis ([[William Grant Craib|Craib]]) Y.Y.Fang & C.Z.Zheng
